description: The plot illustrates Pass@8 accuracy as a function of temperature. The x-axis is labeled “Temperature” with a linear scale ranging from 0.1 to 1.0, with tick labels at intervals of 0.1. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy (Pass@8)” with a linear scale ranging from 62.5 to 80.0, with tick labels at intervals of 2.5. A yellow line, marked with triangle symbols, represents “On-policy RL”, beginning at approximately 63.0 at a temperature of 0.1 and increasing to 75.0 at a temperature of 0.8, then decreasing slightly to 73.0 at a temperature of 1.0. A red line, marked with star symbols, represents “LUFFY”, starting at 76.0 at a temperature of 0.1, rising to a peak of 81.0 at a temperature of 0.8, and remaining at 80.0 at a temperature of 1.0. A teal line, marked with inverted triangle symbols, represents “SFT”, beginning at 73.0 at a temperature of 0.1, decreasing to 68.0 at a temperature of 0.5, and increasing to 74.0 at a temperature of 1.0.
caption_used: The line plot illustrates Pass@8 accuracy across varying generation temperatures, measured on the merged sets of AIME 2024 and AMC. The 'On-policy RL' line (yellow, triangle markers) shows a steady increase from approximately 63.0 at 0.1 to 75.0 at 0.8, followed by a slight decline to 73.0 at 1.0. The 'LUFFY' line (red, star markers) demonstrates consistent superiority, starting at 76.0 at 0.1 and peaking at 81.0 at 0.8, before stabilizing at 80.0 at 1.0. The 'SFT' line (teal, inverted triangle markers) begins at 73.0 at 0.1, dips sharply to 68.0 at 0.5, and recovers to 74.0 at 1.0, showing the most variability among the three methods. Overall, LUFFY consistently outperforms the other methods across all temperature settings, with On-policy RL showing the most significant improvement over time.
